question.problem:
Which of the three sequences below are geometric sequences?

- $5,\,10,\,15,\,…$
- ${a}_{n+1}=6{a}_{n},\,{a}_{1}=18,\,n\ge 1$
- $f(n+1)=2f(n)+3,\,f(1)=1,\,n\ge 1$
question.worked_solution:
A sequence is geometric if there is a common ratio between its terms. Let's check each sequence in turn.

- Sequence I is not geometric because not every pair of consecutive terms has the same ratio. To see this, we only need to go up to the third term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{f(2)}{f(1)}=\frac{10}{5} & =2 \\ \frac{f(3)}{f(2)}=\frac{15}{10} & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- Sequence II is a geometric sequence. The recursive rule ${a}_{n+1}=6{a}_{n}$ tells us that each term is $6$ times the previous term, so the common ratio is $r=6.$

- Sequence III is not a geometric sequence. To see this, we can calculate the first $3$ terms of the sequence and then compute the ratios of consecutive terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =1 \\ f(2) & =2\cdot 1+3=5 \\ f(3) & =2\cdot 5+3=13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first two pairs of consecutive terms have different ratios:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{f(2)}{f(1)}=\frac{5}{1} & =5 \\ \frac{f(3)}{f(2)}=\frac{13}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, only sequence II is a geometric sequence.
